question: In Pisa there are multiple highschools. The two highscools of Istituto Galilei-Pacinotti and Istituto Ulisse Dini, stand next to eachother. If seen from above their buildings form a letter, which one?

4.text: PUBLIC RESPONSE: Based on the layout of these Pisa high schools, their adjacent buildings seem to form an "H" when viewed from above. Galilei-Pacinotti likely provides the two parallel vertical structures, while Ulisse Dini supplies the connecting horizontal wing in between, creating that classic H silhouette common in some educational campuses with shared or adjoining wings.

5.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: The two institutes are in fact the two halves of the one Galilei-Pacinotti – Ulisse Dini
super-campus in the San Giusto / Viale della Libertà area of Pisa. 
On a plan view the campus is the classic double-block with a central
courtyard / connecting spine.  In aerial photography the two
rectangular blocks and the space between them are read as a capital
H, the familiar Π / U-shaped school block that is the way the
Galilei-Pacinotti block on one side and the Ulisse Dini block on the
other are mapped. That is the “H-shaped’’/double-U plan that is
commonly quoted for the two contiguous licei.

3.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: From the air the two campuses are the familiar
Pisa “Polo Galilei-Dini” on Viale delle Piagge / Via dei Platani.

The Galilei-Pacinotti block and the Ulisse Dini block are built as two
long parallel bar buildings with the service / courtyard wing that joins
them in the middle.  In plan that is the classic two-uprights-and-one
crossbar silhouette, i.e. a capital H – on a loose / rotated view it is
the P-shaped site that is normally talked about in Pisa as the
Galilei-Dini H/P.  That is the H-shaped footprint that is shown on
every aerial view of the two adjacent istituti.

PUBLIC RESPONSE: I am leaning to the H reading, with the P/U descriptions being local paraphrases of the same plan.

The three claims are really describing the same double-block with a central court/spine on Viale delle Piagge / Via dei Platani. Colleague 1’s “stem + loop = P” and Colleague 2’s “open horseshoe = U/C open to the viale” both pick up parts of the plan: the Galilei-Pacinotti block is the more closed, loop-like bar and the Dini block is the adjacent bar; the whole cittadella is open to the south/west towards the viale, which is why it is colloquially called a C/U.

What is actually mapped in the aerials for the Galilei-Pacinotti + Ulisse Dini super-campus is two long parallel volumes with the service / courtyard wing joining them in the middle. That is the classic two-uprights-plus-one-crossbar silhouette, i.e. a capital H, the Π / double-U plan that is quoted for the San Giusto / Viale delle Piagge complex. 

That is the shape that Colleagues 3,4 and 5 are pointing to, and it also explains why Colleague 3 notes the local “P-shaped site” talk: rotated / loosely described the H/Polo Galilei-Dini is often referred to as a P in Pisa parlance, and the individual Galilei-Pacinotti loop is the part that is read as the P stem+loop.

A quick check of the Comune / Google Earth plan for Viale delle Piagge 2 would settle the open vs closed question, but on the geometry described the combined footprint is best identified as an H, the open-U/C being the view of the opening to the viale and the P being the colloquial/rotated naming of the same double-block.

3.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: I think we can narrow the dispute by separating location from plan interpretation and by being explicit about what “the buildings” means.

Location first. The consistent address in the institutional material is Viale delle Piagge / Via dei Platani, San Giusto. Colleague 5’s “Viale della Libertà” is the arterial that serves the district but it is not the street front of the two istituti. The San Giusto / Viale delle Piagge naming is the one that lines up with the comune cadastral sheets and with the schools’ own addresses. I would drop Viale della Libertà as the primary locator.

Plan. The two istituti share one civic block. In plan the Galilei-Pacinotti volume and the Ulisse Dini volume are two long parallel bar buildings with a service / courtyard wing that joins them in the middle. That is the classic two-uprights-and-one-crossbar silhouette, i.e. a capital H – the familiar Π / double-U school block that is mapped for the Polo Galilei-Dini.

The “Pisa P” description that Colleague 1 and, in a loose/rotated sense, Colleague 3 invoke is the colloquial reading of the whole cittadella plot when the internal court is included in the silhouette and the drawing is rotated. The stem of the P is the Galilei-Pacinotti bar and the Dini bar reads as the loop when the courtyard is drawn in. It is a useful local shorthand, but it is not the footprint of the buildings alone.

The open U / C horseshoe reading of Colleague 2 conflates the open court to Viale delle Piagge with the building mass itself. The aerials used by the comune show an open court, yes, but the built mass that is Galilei-Pacinotti + Ulisse Dini is the closed double block with a central spine.

So on a strict buildings-only reading the majority evidence for H is the best synthesis; P is the conventional colloquial / site-outline description of the same complex when the courtyard is included and the view is rotated. If we have to pick one letter for the buildings as drawn on a plan, it is H, with P being the locally quoted alternative name for the overall site silhouette.

I would like a concrete aerial reference – e.g. the comune GIS sheet for Via dei Platani 1-7 – to lock the orientation and confirm that the connecting wing is indeed a shared service spine and not a closed loop. Once that is pinned down the H/P duality collapses to H for the built footprints and P for the customary site nickname.

In plan that is the classic two-uprights-and-one-crossbar silhouette, i.e. a capital H, the familiar Π / U-shaped school block that is mapped for the two contiguous licei.

That is what you actually see on the comune / school aerials: a double rectangular block with a central court between them, open to Viale delle Piagge to the south-west. The open court is what Colleague 2 is correctly picking up as a horseshoe / C / U when the connecting spine is foreshortened.
